liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Let The Good Times Roll** (4 reviews): Jerry smiled throughout this opener, which the writer calls a breakout; First-ever performance of this soul number; Bobby oversang it right away [13][18][20][23]
- **Hey Pocky Way** (1 review, 1 other source): Bobby announced it as a drummers' choice; Noted as a drummers' choice [8][18]
- **Feel Like A Stranger** (1 review): Followed the opener and was very danceable [15]
- **Row Jimmy** (1 review): Jerry's voice sounded smooth and much better than much of spring 1988 [18]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Closed the first set [15]
- **Shakedown Street** (1 review): Second-set version contained a jam with notably sweet, old-fashioned playing [15]
- **Black Peter** (1 review): Judged more intense than the Watchtower [16]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 review): Bobby's guitar failed during the climax; visibly frustrated, he gave up and the song ended abruptly [14]

## Setlist highlights

- Earliest performances in the archive: Let The Good Times Roll [25]

## The recordings

- **gd88-04-30.matrix.lemon2.4664.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 151 min; rated 4.08/5 by 13 [1]. Said about its sound: An early-90s online review praised the sound and Brent's strong performance [22]
- **gd1988-04-30.164175.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 150 min [5]
- **gd1988-04-30.145595.fob.nak700.anon.noel.t-flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 155 min [8]
- **gd88-04-30.prefm.lai.3394.sbeok.shnf**: pre-FM broadcast master; 20 songs; 145 min; rated 3.87/5 by 15 [10]. Said about its sound: Reviewer found the sound excellent; Reviewer recalls Brent sounding great and the sound quality as fantastic [21][24]

## Around the show

- Venue had oak trees and eucalyptus scent; the front row always had space to move [13]
- An unusually long wait came before the encore, longer than the usual few minutes [14]
- Reviewer brought family and friends for a picnic-like day and smuggled in oysters with a horseradish bottle [16]
- Reportedly second-set sound problems led to the extra mini encore set as compensation [20]
- Encore was China Cat Sunflower into I Know You Rider into One More Saturday Night [1]
- Bobby's anger at his gear recalls the pay-per-view Summer Solstice show, where he kicked his rack [14]
- Rest of the show is solid rather than spectacular, with no clunkers [23]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd88-04-30.matrix.lemon2.4664.sbeok.shnf**: source: Healy Ultramatrix [1]. Also: Reviewer first got the show on two XLII cassettes, sent by a poster from the Dead flames usergroup; Source is a Healy Ultramatrix, circulated via lemon2 and childo [1][22]
- **gd1988-04-30.164175.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Bob Wagner's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony D5M (Maxell UDXLII-S90) [5]. Also: A Superscope EC7 source from Jeff Bowen patches 30 seconds in Space; A Uher audience source from Danny T and Tommy McKeown patches 11 seconds in the Rider to Saturday Night transition [5]
- **gd1988-04-30.145595.fob.nak700.anon.noel.t-flac16**: taped by Anon; transferred by Joe Noel; source: Lineage: Nakamichi 700 cardioids front of board -> tcd5m (master) -> Korg mr1000 (1 bit, 5.6 Mhz) -> render in AudioGate to 24 bits 48 khz sampling. [8]. Also: Patches come from Superscope EC-7 and Uher 240 deck sources, courtesy of Jeff Bowen and Danny T; A tape flip in the first set was cross-faded [8]
- **gd88-04-30.prefm.lai.3394.sbeok.shnf**: source: Pre-FM> Reel> Cassette> cdr [10]. Also: Reviewer got a tape around 1993 from someone on the Dead flames newsgroup [24]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Frost 1988](https://www.dead.net/fanphotos/frost-1988) [26]
- Poster by Wolfgang's: [Grateful Dead Laminate from Frost Amphitheatre, Apr 30, 1988 at Wolfgang's](https://www.wolfgangs.com/backstage-passes/grateful-dead/laminate/FRA880430.html) [27]
- Poster by Kirsten Michel: [1988-04-30 Frost Amphitheatre, Palo Alto, CA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1988-04-30-frost-amphitheatre-palo-alto-ca-usa/) [28]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Legendary FM Broadcasts - Frost Amphitheater, Stanford Univesity 30th April 1988](https://www.deezer.com/en/album/14115184) [29]
- Poster by thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead - 1988-04-30 Frost Amphitheatre, Stanford University, Palo Alto, CA](https://thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com/2018/08/grateful-dead-1988-04-30-frost.html) [30]
